Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Edit files there directly. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no external capture.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching a file outside the owned list, changing production code with no tests, fewer than 4 new def test_..., no negative test (pytest.raises / assert ... is False / assert-not-equal proving the OLD behavior is gone), or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these):
  server/pipeline/angle_editor.py
  tests/test_angle_editor.py
  tests/test_angle_editor_dominant_hold.py

OWNER RULE, now ABSOLUTE: the shown camera must ALWAYS follow the loudest speaker (isolated-mic margin >= 6dB). No exceptions, including the outro.

THE BUG, confirmed by an independent review at 98% confidence. In server/pipeline/angle_editor.py the run-smoothing absorbs ANY run shorter than min_run_s (1.2s) into the neighbouring run as backchannel de-bounce. There are TWO such sites: line ~85-86 (`if merged and ln < min_frames: merged[-1][2] += ln`) in frames_to_turns, and line ~143-145 (`cur[1] = en  # absorb short shot; hold current angle`) in the downstream smoothing. Both have the same defect: a brief but DOMINANT host or guest speech run gets absorbed into the OTHER speaker's camera. A real render showed the guest camera for the final 5.5s while the host was 14.7dB louder, because the host's short closing run was absorbed backward into the preceding guest run.

WHY host/guest runs are always real dominant speech (so this is safe): classify_frames only labels a frame 'host' or 'guest' when that track LEADS the other by >= margin_db (6dB). A quiet backchannel ('mm-hm') while the other person talks does NOT lead by 6dB, so it is never labelled as the backchanneler; it stays as the dominant speaker or 'two'. Therefore a 'host' or 'guest' run is, by construction, genuine dominant speech and must be shown. Only 'sbs' (from 'two'/crosstalk) and silence-held runs are ambiguous and may be debounced.

THE FIX (implement exactly this, at BOTH absorption sites): only absorb a short run when its angle is 'sbs'. NEVER absorb a 'host' or 'guest' run into a different angle. Concretely, the absorb condition becomes: absorb only if (run is shorter than min_frames) AND (the short run's angle == 'sbs' OR the short run's angle == the neighbour it would merge into). A short 'host' or 'guest' run whose neighbour is a DIFFERENT angle must be kept as its own turn even if it is shorter than min_run_s. Apply the identical guard to the second site (~line 143-145). Keep the existing 'sil' hold-previous behaviour and the 'two'->'sbs' mapping unchanged.

ACCEPTANCE (the review's exact criterion): a short host or guest run must NEVER be merged into the opposite speaker; a short 'sbs' run may still debounce; a short run adjacent to the SAME angle still coalesces normally.

This may produce a brief (<1.2s) cut to the dominant speaker where before it was suppressed. That is CORRECT per the absolute owner rule and is accepted. Do not add a special case for the final segment; the general rule covers it.

TESTS (in tests/test_angle_editor_dominant_hold.py): prove (1) the exact failing pattern -- a long guest run followed by a short (<1.2s) host run at the END -- now yields a final HOST turn, not guest (this is the regression that was shipping); (2) a short 'sbs' run between two host runs is still absorbed; (3) a short host run BETWEEN two guest runs survives as its own host turn (negative test: assert the result is NOT all-guest / assert host appears); (4) a short run adjacent to the SAME angle still coalesces. Also confirm both smoothing sites behave consistently. Pure unit tests on the functions; no ffmpeg, no media.
